newsitem.title: USA: King is first to Iditarod halfway point.
newsitem.headline: King is first to Iditarod halfway point.

text.p: Defending champion Jeff King was the first to reach the halfway point in the Iditarod Trail Sled Dog Race Thursday and earned a prize of $3,000 in gold nuggets.
King, who won the 1,161-mile race in 1993 and 1996, arrived at the abandoned mining settlement of Iditarod at 4:06 p.m. (8:06 p.m. EST), 37 minutes ahead of two-time champion Martin Buser.
Doug Swingley, the 1995 champion of the Anchorage-to-Nome race, was third to reach Iditarod, arriving at 4:50 p.m. (8:50 p.m. EST), race officials said.
No other mushers had reached Iditarod by late Thursday afternoon, officials said.
Meanwhile, searchers located a British musher who had been missing for nearly two days on a windswept, 93-mile stretch of the race course.

Max Hall, of Manchester, England, was spotted headed into the Athabaskan Indian village of Nikolai, 365 miles into the course. The 46-year-old businessman told officials he had taken a wrong turn but intended to stay in the race.
Also Thursday, a third dog was reported dead.
The Iditarod began Saturday with a ceremonial run in Anchorage. Timed competition began Sunday in Willow.
In the past two years, Iditarod champions have reached the Nome finish line in nine days. The winner gets $50,000 and a new truck, part of the total race purse of over $400,000.
Of the 53 mushers who began the Iditarod, three had dropped out as of Thursday.
